x_1577958_dsb_pattern.name: Platform upgrade, customisation and technical-debt remediation
x_1577958_dsb_pattern.overview: Measure, triage, protect, then upgrade on a cadence. (1) Run evidence on a fresh production clone: release history, skipped records, customisation footprint, Instance Scan and ATF coverage. (2) Triage every skipped record and customised OOB file with a four-way disposition — revert to base, merge (retain with the new baseline changes), retain as justified customisation, or retire — owned by the relevant process owner. (3) Build the safety net before touching code: ATF suites for the critical journeys, scheduled Instance Scan with agreed suites. (4) Remediate in waves by application, reverting first because it removes future upgrade cost. (5) Replace deprecated features and legacy workflows with Flow Designer and current plugins per the release notes. (6) Upgrade using the documented clone → upgrade → ATF → UAT → promote runbook, with Upgrade Center / Upgrade Plan where available. (7) Hold the line with development standards, peer review and scan gates on update sets. Report the debt trend monthly.
x_1577958_dsb_pattern.pain: Upgrades take months and are deferred; the instance falls out of support Thousands of skipped records with no owner or decision Customised OOB scripts break silently after each upgrade No regression automation; testing is manual and incomplete Deprecated plugins and legacy workflows block new capabilities
x_1577958_dsb_pattern.summary: The instance is one or more family releases behind because every upgrade is painful: thousands of skipped records, heavy customisation of OOB scripts and forms, legacy workflows, and no automated regression. The pattern converges on a repeatable upgrade capability: evidence-based debt inventory (skipped records, customer updates, Instance Scan findings, deprecated features), a triage decision per item (revert to OOB, retain and merge, rebuild, or retire), an ATF regression suite for critical journeys, and a clone-upgrade-test cadence that keeps the instance within N-1.
